behaviors.v1Behavior: Known item IDs are accepted by the production boundary.
behaviors.expectedV2: Known active item IDs are accepted by scoreAssessment.

behaviors.v1Behavior: Duplicate production responses are retained deterministically after sorting.
behaviors.expectedV2: Duplicate raw response IDs fail closed with a structured input error.

behaviors.v1Behavior: Production scoring is versioned by its contract and scoring metadata.
behaviors.expectedV2: Response, content, scoring, result, and research versions remain independently bound.

behaviors.v1Behavior: Unknown request fields are generally ignored by legacy callers.
behaviors.expectedV2: Assessment input has an exact-key fail-closed contract.

behaviors.v1Behavior: Missing evidence does not create a scored production value.
behaviors.expectedV2: Missing responses are explicit, excluded from contribution, and increase abstention evidence.

behaviors.v1Behavior: Legacy answer maps did not distinguish every non-answer state.
behaviors.expectedV2: Skipped is a first-class non-scored state distinct from missing, refusal, and abstention.

behaviors.v1Behavior: Refusal does not contribute a neutral value.
behaviors.expectedV2: Refusal is excluded and produces explicit refusal uncertainty.

behaviors.v1Behavior: Dont-know-like answers are non-scored.
behaviors.expectedV2: Explicit abstention is excluded and preserved in evidence records.

behaviors.v1Behavior: Likert 5 values normalize to the signed unit interval.
behaviors.expectedV2: Likert 5 uses value / 2 before reverse scoring.

behaviors.v1Behavior: Likert 7 values normalize to the signed unit interval.
behaviors.expectedV2: Likert 7 uses value / 3 before reverse scoring.

behaviors.v1Behavior: Reverse scoring inverts one normalized response.
behaviors.expectedV2: Reverse scoring is applied once after scale conversion.

behaviors.v1Behavior: The production adapter accepts already normalized values.
behaviors.expectedV2: Raw v2 Likert values are legal integers only and out-of-range values fail closed.

behaviors.v1Behavior: The selected statement option supplies direct construct values.
behaviors.expectedV2: The selected option owns the complete explicit contribution mapping.

behaviors.v1Behavior: Historical option fallback could inherit item-level or neighboring mappings.
behaviors.expectedV2: Missing option mappings are a compile-time/content-validation failure.

behaviors.v1Behavior: Descriptive confidence scales influence from 0.2 through 1.
behaviors.expectedV2: Confidence uses the same explicit 1, 3, 5 mapping.

behaviors.v1Behavior: Prescriptive priority scales influence from 0.2 through 1.
behaviors.expectedV2: Priority uses the same explicit 1, 3, 5 mapping.

behaviors.v1Behavior: Normative responses have neutral salience.
behaviors.expectedV2: Normative responses always use salience 1.

behaviors.v1Behavior: A legacy salience omission could be treated as ordinary neutral evidence.
behaviors.expectedV2: salienceSkipped excludes non-normative contribution and is visible in evidence.

behaviors.v1Behavior: Signed item-to-dimension weights determine contribution direction and magnitude.
behaviors.expectedV2: Explicit polarity and absolute weight determine one contribution record.

behaviors.v1Behavior: An item can affect multiple measured dimensions.
behaviors.expectedV2: Each explicit mapping contributes independently with its own evidence.

behaviors.v1Behavior: Fallback mapping could manufacture a contribution from an item construct list.
behaviors.expectedV2: No fallback mapping exists; the compiler rejects an unmapped scored item.

behaviors.v1Behavior: Dimension scores are bounded weighted aggregates.
behaviors.expectedV2: Construct score is clamp(sum(weighted contributions) / sum(abs weights)).

behaviors.v1Behavior: Dimension evidence is based on answered mapped items.
behaviors.expectedV2: Construct evidence tracks answered, eligible, mapped, and salience coverage separately.

behaviors.v1Behavior: Legacy no-evidence dimensions could expose numeric zero.
behaviors.expectedV2: No evidence is null/abstained, never an interpreted neutral score.

behaviors.v1Behavior: Only answered evidence contributes to an aggregate.
behaviors.expectedV2: Missing, skipped, refused, and abstained records have zero effective contribution.

behaviors.v1Behavior: Labels compare against declared centroid dimensions.
behaviors.expectedV2: Profiles compare only against explicit profile requirements.

behaviors.v1Behavior: Required evidence gates prevent unsupported label exposure.
behaviors.expectedV2: Constitutive gates are explicit and evaluated before ranking.

behaviors.v1Behavior: Profile fit is monotonic with declared centroid distance.
behaviors.expectedV2: Distance is normalized RMS Euclidean distance and similarity is bounded.

behaviors.v1Behavior: Equal top fits are deterministic.
behaviors.expectedV2: Tie tolerance and explicit label-tie uncertainty are stable.

behaviors.v1Behavior: Ranked label output is deterministic.
behaviors.expectedV2: Profile ranking sorts by score then stable ID.

behaviors.v1Behavior: Modifier matches share parts of the label/result path.
behaviors.expectedV2: Modifiers are separate content and result records, not primary profiles.

behaviors.v1Behavior: Modifier evidence thresholds filter unsupported matches.
behaviors.expectedV2: Minimum indicator evidence and fit thresholds are explicit.

behaviors.v1Behavior: Unavailable follow-up modifiers may be absent from ordinary output.
behaviors.expectedV2: Unavailable modifiers remain explicit with status unavailable and reason.

behaviors.v1Behavior: Specialist assignment and scoring were coupled to runtime module code.
behaviors.expectedV2: Activation is explicit input plus content-defined module policy.

behaviors.v1Behavior: Specialist items belong to a module and module-specific constructs.
behaviors.expectedV2: Every specialist item and construct resolves through an explicit module.

behaviors.v1Behavior: Specialist profiles are scored within specialist modules.
behaviors.expectedV2: Module output profiles have explicit requirements, gates, and provenance.

behaviors.v1Behavior: Specialist evidence could contaminate core result paths.
behaviors.expectedV2: Specialist evidence is module-scoped and never changes core constructs.

behaviors.v1Behavior: Explanations identify contributing dimensions.
behaviors.expectedV2: Diagnostics point to the same immutable contribution records used for scores.

behaviors.v1Behavior: Cross-layer divergence is reportable.
behaviors.expectedV2: Explicit diagnostic relations drive divergence summaries.

behaviors.v1Behavior: Domain summaries are explanatory projections.
behaviors.expectedV2: Domain diagnostics consume scored records without rescoring.

behaviors.v1Behavior: Historical diagnostic paths could recalculate scores.
behaviors.expectedV2: Diagnostics cannot invoke normalization, aggregation, or profile matching.

behaviors.v1Behavior: Content and scoring metadata identify the result provenance.
behaviors.expectedV2: All result layers carry independent version fields and content fingerprint.

behaviors.v1Behavior: The same input and canonical source are deterministic.
behaviors.expectedV2: Compilation, scoring, serialization, and fingerprints are byte deterministic.

behaviors.v1Behavior: Legacy result payload combines multiple scoring surfaces.
behaviors.expectedV2: One immutable AssessmentResult is the only v2 result contract.

behaviors.v1Behavior: Legacy and production scoring could both execute for one result.
behaviors.expectedV2: Dual scoring is forbidden; scoreAssessment has one ordered authority chain.

behaviors.v1Behavior: Mapping fallbacks manufacture semantic authority.
behaviors.expectedV2: Fallback mapping names and behavior are absent from v2 runtime.

behaviors.v1Behavior: Overlay history can apply reverse corrections more than once.
behaviors.expectedV2: Reverse polarity is represented once in content and applied once in normalization.

behaviors.v1Behavior: Legacy type projections can become an accidental scoring authority.
behaviors.expectedV2: v2 engine contracts are canonical and do not import legacy Question/Axis/Label types.

behaviors.v1Behavior: Historical aliases can enter active scoring through compatibility selectors.
behaviors.expectedV2: Retired and compatibility labels stay outside active scoring content.

behaviors.v1Behavior: Generated canonical TS can be edited as source authority.
behaviors.expectedV2: Generated output is immutable and source content owns semantics.

behaviors.v1Behavior: Reliability terminology can stand in for evidence validity.
behaviors.expectedV2: v2 exposes evidence and uncertainty, not reliability labels.

behaviors.v1Behavior: Unanswered items can be interpreted as neutral zero.
behaviors.expectedV2: Unanswered items are abstention/evidence states and never neutral scores.

behaviors.v1Behavior: Gate failure and unavailable evidence can collapse into one result.
behaviors.expectedV2: Gate failed and gate unavailable are distinct statuses/reasons.

behaviors.v1Behavior: Specialist evidence can be merged into core scoring.
behaviors.expectedV2: Specialist contamination is prevented by module-scoped content indexes.

behaviors.v1Behavior: Diagnostics may rescore to explain a result.
behaviors.expectedV2: Diagnostic records reference authoritative outputs and never rescore.

behaviors.v1Behavior: Historical overlay files can remain independently editable authorities.
behaviors.expectedV2: A semantic fact has one canonical owner in v2 content.
